title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON MANAGEMENT CONSULTANTS AND TECHNICAL CONSULTANTS
title_original: 경영지도사 및 기술지도사에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON MANAGEMENT CONSULTANTS AND TECHNICAL CONSULTANTS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Management Consultants and Technical Consultants and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Scope of Statutes and Regulations concerning Small and Medium Enterprises)
The scope of statutes and regulations concerning small and medium enterprises under Article 2 (2) 6 and (3) 3 of the Act on Management Consultants and Technical Consultants (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") shall be as specified in attached Table 1.

Article 3 (Consultant Qualification Examination)
(1) The subjects of the first and second stages of the consultant qualification examination under Article 5 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "consultant qualification examination") shall be as specified in attached Table 2.
(2) The first stage of the consultant qualification examination shall be a written examination with objective questions, and the second stage shall be a written examination with subjective questions.
(3) The English subject among the first-stage examination subjects shall be replaced by a score obtained in an English proficiency test specified in attached Table 3 (hereinafter referred to as an "English test" in this Article), among English proficiency tests conducted on or after January 1 of the year containing the date that falls five years before the closing date for receipt of applications for the relevant examination (limited to scores announced by the closing date for receipt of applications for the first-stage examination and confirmed by the method specified in the public notice under Article 4 (2)). <Amended on March 26, 2024>
(4) The passing criteria for the first-stage examination in subjects other than English and for the second-stage examination shall be at least 40 points in each subject and an average of at least 60 points across all subjects, with a maximum of 100 points for each subject.
(5) A person intending to take the consultant qualification examination shall submit an English test score report together with the application form.
(6) The Minister of SMEs and Startups shall issue to persons who pass the consultant qualification examination a consultant qualification certificate prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups.

Article 4 (Scope of Duties of Examination Administering Institutions, etc.)
(1) The scope of duties of an examination administering institution designated under Article 5 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "examination administering institution") shall be as follows:
1. Public announcement of the consultant qualification examination;
2. Distribution and receipt of application forms for the consultant qualification examination;
3. Administration of the consultant qualification examination and activities incidental thereto.
(2) To administer the consultant qualification examination, an examination administering institution shall determine the date, time, and place of the examination, the scope of questions for each examination subject, the distribution and receipt of application forms, examination fees, and other matters necessary for administering the examination, obtain approval from the Minister of SMEs and Startups, and publicly announce those matters on its website, etc. no later than 90 days before the examination date.

Article 5 (Examination Fees)
(1) The fee under Article 5 (4) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "examination fee") shall be determined by the examination administering institution, with approval from the Minister of SMEs and Startups, within the actual expenses necessary for administering the consultant qualification examination.
(2) Upon receiving a request for approval of examination fees from an examination administering institution under paragraph (1), the Minister of SMEs and Startups shall grant approval after gathering the opinions of interested parties.
(3) The Minister of SMEs and Startups who approves examination fees under paragraph (2) shall post the details of the approval on the website of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, etc.
(4) Where a person intending to take the consultant qualification examination (hereinafter referred to as an "applicant" in this paragraph) falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the examination administering institution shall refund all or part of the examination fee as specified in the relevant subparagraph:
1. Where an examination fee is paid in error or in excess: The entire amount paid in error or in excess;
2. Where the applicant is unable to take the examination for a reason attributable to the examination administering institution: The entire examination fee paid by the applicant;
3. Where the applicant cancels the application during the application period: The entire examination fee paid by the applicant;
4. Where the applicant cancels the application between the day following the closing date for receipt of applications and 20 days before the examination date: 60 percent of the examination fee paid by the applicant;
5. Where the applicant cancels the application between 19 days and 10 days before the examination date: 50 percent of the examination fee paid by the applicant;
6. Where the applicant is unable to take the examination because the applicant's spouse, or a parent, paternal grandparent, maternal grandparent, sibling, or child of the applicant or the applicant's spouse, dies during the period from seven days before the examination date through the examination date: 50 percent of the examination fee paid by the applicant;
7. Where the applicant is unable to take the examination because of hospitalization due to an accident or illness (limited to cases where the examination date falls within the hospitalization period): 50 percent of the examination fee paid by the applicant;
8. Where the applicant is unable to take the examination because the applicant is quarantined due to infection with, or the risk of infection with, a Class 1 infectious disease under subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act or a Class 2 infectious disease under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of that Act: The entire examination fee paid by the applicant;
9. Where an applicant who is a member of the military or a civilian military employee is unable to take the examination because leave, outings, etc. are prohibited under the control of the head of an agency affiliated with the Ministry of National Defense, the commander of a unit under the Ministry's direct control, or the commander of a unit belonging to any branch of the armed forces: The entire examination fee paid by the applicant.

Article 6 (Practical Training)
(1) The practical training (hereinafter referred to as "practical training") that a person qualified as a management consultant or technical consultant (hereinafter referred to as a "consultant") must complete to register as a consultant pursuant to the former part of Article 8 (1) of the Act shall be at least 100 hours: Provided, That the duration of practical training for persons falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 6 (1) of the Act and persons who have completed the consultant training course under Article 22 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "consultant training course") may be set at not less than 60 hours.
(2) Practical training shall be provided by a designated educational institution designated under Article 23 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "practical training institution").
(3) Practical training shall consist of a job-related education course and a practical education course, and its contents and methods shall be as specified in attached Table 4.
(4) A practical training institution shall consult with the Minister of SMEs and Startups when determining the detailed contents, duration, costs, and other matters necessary for practical training.
(5) A practical training institution shall issue a certificate of completion of practical training prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups to a person who has completed practical training and report the results to the Minister of SMEs and Startups.

Article 7 (Registration of Consultants)
(1) A person who intends to register to commence work as a consultant pursuant to the former part of Article 8 (1) of the Act shall submit to the Minister of SMEs and Startups an application for registration as a consultant prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, attaching the following documents:
1. One photograph (taken within the preceding six months and measuring 3.5 centimeters in width and 4.5 centimeters in height);
2. A copy of the certificate of completion of practical training.
(2) Upon receiving an application for registration as a consultant under paragraph (1), the Minister of SMEs and Startups shall issue a consultant registration certificate prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, except where a ground for refusal of registration specified in the subparagraphs of Article 9 (1) of the Act applies.

Article 8 (Renewal of Registration of Consultants)
(1) The Minister of SMEs and Startups shall inform a person registered as a consultant under Article 8 (1) of the Act of the procedures for applying for renewal of registration under Article 8 (2) of the Act, by written document, mobile phone text message, email, telephone, etc., no later than 60 days before five years elapse from the date of registration as a consultant.
(2) A consultant who intends to renew registration pursuant to the former part of Article 8 (2) of the Act shall apply to the Minister of SMEs and Startups for renewal of registration, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, no later than 30 days before five years elapse from the date of registration as a consultant.
(3) "Special reasons prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as natural disasters or a long-term stay abroad" in the proviso to Article 8 (2) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where a person is unable to perform duties as a consultant due to war, fire, natural disaster, infectious disease, or another equivalent disaster;
2. Where a person stays abroad for at least 90 days for the purposes of performing duties and developing competencies, including official business, training, research, and technical guidance;
3. Other cases in which the Minister of SMEs and Startups recognizes grounds equivalent to those specified in subparagraphs 1 and 2.

Article 9 (Disclosure of Information)
(1) The scope of information disclosed under Article 13 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Name;
2. Office address and telephone number;
3. Field in which the qualification was acquired and date of acquisition;
4. Date of registration as a consultant;
5. Status of business commencement or suspension, and the dates of commencement or suspension;
6. Areas of specialization, career experience, etc. and information that can substantiate them;
7. Other information related to the engagement of a consultant that the consultant has consented to disclose.
(2) Information under Article 13 (1) of the Act shall be disclosed by posting it on the website of the corporation designated by the Minister of SMEs and Startups pursuant to the former part of paragraph (2) of the same Article.

Article 10 (Operation of Consultant Training Courses, etc.)
(1) A person seeking designation as an institution responsible for consultant training courses under Article 22 (1) of the Act shall meet the following designation criteria and apply to the Minister of SMEs and Startups for designation:
1. The person shall be a corporation;
2. The person shall have the specialized personnel and facilities determined and publicly notified by the Minister of SMEs and Startups.
(2) An institution responsible for consultant training courses designated under Article 22 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "consultant training institution") shall operate consultant training courses separately as management consultant training courses and technical consultant training courses in accordance with the educational standards for consultant training courses in attached Table 5.
(3) A consultant training institution shall consult with the Minister of SMEs and Startups when determining the contents, duration, costs, and other matters necessary for consultant training courses.
(4) A consultant training institution shall administer a consultant training course completion examination to persons who have completed a consultant training course and shall issue a certificate of completion of the consultant training course prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups to persons who pass that examination.
(5) When a consultant training institution has provided education for a consultant training course, it shall report the results of that education to the Minister of SMEs and Startups within 30 days from the date the education ends.

Article 11 (Eligibility Requirements for Participants in Consultant Training Courses)
(1) Persons eligible to attend consultant training courses under Article 22 (2) of the Act shall be the following: <Amended on August 9, 2022>
1. Persons holding a doctoral degree or recognized under statutes and regulations as having educational attainment at least equivalent thereto, who have at least five years of experience related to diagnosis and guidance after acquiring the degree or obtaining recognition of their educational attainment;
2. Persons holding a master's degree or recognized under statutes and regulations as having educational attainment at least equivalent thereto, who have at least seven years of experience related to diagnosis and guidance after acquiring the degree or obtaining recognition of their educational attainment;
3. University graduates or persons recognized under statutes and regulations as having educational attainment at least equivalent thereto, who have at least nine years of experience related to diagnosis and guidance after acquiring the degree or obtaining recognition of their educational attainment;
4. Junior college graduates or persons recognized under statutes and regulations as having educational attainment at least equivalent thereto, who have at least 11 years of experience related to diagnosis and guidance after acquiring the degree or obtaining recognition of their educational attainment;
5. Persons with at least five years of experience related to diagnosis and guidance at the Ministry of SMEs and Startups or a guidance institution designated under Article 44 (1) of the Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Act.
(2) Degrees, educational attainment, and experience related to diagnosis and guidance under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) shall be limited to those related to the matters specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (2) and the subparagraphs of paragraph (3) of the same Article of the Act.
(3) A person who intends to attend a consultant training course shall submit documents proving the qualifications specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) to the consultant training institution before the consultant training course begins.

Article 12 (Criteria for Designating Educational Institutions, etc.)
(1) The criteria for designation of designated educational institutions under Article 23 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. The institution shall be a corporation;
2. The institution shall have the specialized personnel and facilities determined and publicly notified by the Minister of SMEs and Startups.
(2) Matters necessary for the designation of designated educational institutions, including detailed designation procedures, other than those provided for in paragraph (1), shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of SMEs and Startups.

Article 13 (Registration of Consulting Corporations)
(1) Where a management and technical consulting corporation, management consulting corporation, or technical consulting corporation under Article 24 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "consulting corporation") intends to register under Article 25 (1) of the Act, it shall submit to the Minister of SMEs and Startups an application for registration of a consulting corporation prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, accompanied by the following documents:
1. Articles of incorporation;
2. The resume of the representative director;
3. Copies of consultant registration certificates held by directors and by consultants who are not directors (hereinafter referred to as "affiliated consultants");
4. Documents certifying payment of capital (referring, in the case of cash contributions, to a certificate of payment of capital issued by a bank under the Banking Act and, in the case of contributions in kind, to documents certifying their fulfillment and an appraisal report issued by an accredited appraisal institution).
(2) Upon receiving an application for registration under paragraph (1), the Minister of SMEs and Startups shall enter the consulting corporation in the register of consulting corporations prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, except where the registration requirements under Article 25 (2) of the Act are not met.
(3) Upon registering a consulting corporation under paragraph (2), the Minister of SMEs and Startups shall issue to the applicant a certificate of registration of a consulting corporation prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups.

Article 14 (Representative Director of a Consulting Corporation) Pursuant to Article 26 (5) of the Act, a consulting corporation shall select a director to represent the corporation by resolution of the general meeting of members, unless otherwise provided in its articles of incorporation. In such cases, the general meeting of members may determine that several directors shall jointly represent the corporation.

Article 15 (Accumulation of Damages Reserves, etc.)
(1) Pursuant to Article 28 (1) of the Act, a consulting corporation shall set aside, for each business year, an amount equivalent to 2/100 of its total sales for that business year as a damages reserve, or obtain liability insurance for damages with a coverage limit not less than the amount specified in subparagraph 1 minus the amount specified in subparagraph 2:
1. The amount calculated by multiplying the number of consultants belonging to the consulting corporation by 4 million won;
2. The amount set aside by the consulting corporation as a damages reserve.
(2) A consulting corporation shall accumulate the damages reserve under paragraph (1) until it reaches an amount equivalent to 10/100 of the average total sales for the 2 immediately preceding business years and the current business year.
(3) Where a consulting corporation exercises a right of recourse against a director or an employee, including an affiliated consultant, in connection with the use of its damages reserve, it shall record the amount recovered as part of the damages reserve.
(4) Where a consulting corporation obtains liability insurance for damages under paragraph (1), it shall notify the Minister of SMEs and Startups of that fact with documents evidencing the insurance coverage.

Article 16 (Restrictions on Investments in Other Corporations, etc.) Pursuant to Article 29 (1) of the Act, the aggregate amount invested by a consulting corporation in other corporations and the amount of debts guaranteed by it on behalf of others shall not exceed 50/100 of its equity capital (the amount of debts guaranteed on behalf of others shall not exceed 20/100 of its equity capital). Provided, That, where its equity capital minus its damages reserve exceeds 200 million won, it may invest in other corporations up to an amount equal to the sum of 50/100 of its equity capital and the excess amount.

Article 17 (Application for Authorization to Establish the Association) A person seeking authorization to establish the Association of Management and Technical Consultants (hereinafter referred to as the "Association") pursuant to Article 38 (3) of the Act shall submit to the Minister of SMEs and Startups an application prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, accompanied by the following documents:
1. A list of promoters and their resumes;
2. Articles of incorporation;
3. Documents stating the business plan and the revenue and expenditure budget;
4. Written consents to assume office from persons scheduled to become officers;
5. Minutes of the inaugural general meeting.

Article 18 (Entrustment of Duties)
(1) The Minister of SMEs and Startups shall entrust the following duties to the Association pursuant to Article 41 of the Act:
1. Receipt of applications for registration of consultants and reports on changes under Article 8 (1) of the Act;
2. Receipt of reports on the commencement, suspension, or closure of a consultant's business and reports on the establishment, relocation, or closure of a consultant's office under Article 15 (2) of the Act;
3. Receipt of notices of dissolution of consulting corporations under Article 34 (2) of the Act;
4. Receipt of reports on amendments to the articles of incorporation of consulting corporations under Article 35 of the Act;
5. Provision of guidance on procedures for applying for renewal of registration under Article 8 (1);
6. Receipt of applications for renewal of consultant registration under Article 8 (2);
7. Receipt of applications for registration of consulting corporations under Article 13 (1);
8. Issuance of certificates of registration of consulting corporations under Article 13 (3);
9. Receipt of notices of liability insurance coverage for damages under Article 15 (4).
(2) The Association entrusted with duties under paragraph (1) shall report the results of handling the entrusted duties to the Minister of SMEs and Startups within 15 days from the date on which they are handled.

Article 19 (Processing of Sensitive Information and Unique Identifying Information) Where unavoidable for the performance of the following duties, the Minister of SMEs and Startups (including examination administering institutions and the Association entrusted with the Minister's duties pursuant to Article 18) may process information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act and data containing resident registration numbers or alien registration numbers under subparagraph 1 or 4 of Article 19 of that Decree. Provided, That, for the duties specified in subparagraphs 5 and 6, information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act shall be excluded. <Amended 2022.12.20>
1. Duties concerning consultant qualification examinations under Article 5 of the Act;
2. Duties concerning exemption from the first-stage examination under Article 6 of the Act;
3. Duties concerning receipt of applications for registration of consultants under Article 8 (1) of the Act;
4. Duties concerning receipt of applications for renewal of consultant registration under Article 8 (2) of the Act;
5. Duties concerning receipt of reports on the commencement of a consultant's business or establishment of a consultant's office under Article 15 (2) of the Act;
6. Duties concerning receipt of applications for registration of consulting corporations under Article 25 of the Act.

Article 20 (Review of Regulations) The Minister of SMEs and Startups shall review the appropriateness of the following matters every 3 years from the reference date specified in each subparagraph (meaning that the review shall be completed before the day corresponding to the reference date in every third year) and take measures, including improvements:
1. Matters concerning the accumulation of damages reserves under Article 15: January 1, 2021;
2. Matters concerning restrictions on investments in other corporations under Article 16: January 1, 2021.

Article 21 (Criteria for Imposition of Administrative Fines) The criteria for imposition of administrative fines under Article 44 (1) of the Act shall be as prescribed in Attached Table 6.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 31611, April 6, 2021>

Article 4 (Transitional Measures concerning Eligibility Requirements for Participants in Consultant Training Courses)
A person who satisfies the eligibility requirements for participants in consultant training courses under Article 44 (2) of the previous Enforcement Decree of the Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Act at the time this Decree enters into force shall be deemed to satisfy the eligibility requirements for participants in consultant training courses under Article 11 (1) and (2).

Article 6 (Relationship with Other Statutes and Regulations)
Where other statutes or regulations cite the previous provisions of the Enforcement Decree of the Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Act concerning management consultants and technical consultants at the time this Decree enters into force, and this Decree contains corresponding provisions, they shall be deemed to cite the corresponding provisions of this Decree in place of the previous provisions.
